# Results — Study 337 (Covered-Call-ETF) on the real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Five buy-write "income" ETFs —
the systematic at-the-money writers **QYLD** (on QQQ), **XYLD** (on SPX) and **RYLD** (on
Russell 2000), and the newer actively-managed out-of-the-money / ELN funds **JEPI** and
**JEPQ** — raced against **SPY total return** on aligned monthly bars. Each fund's
distribution is decomposed into a **price** leg (NAV) and a **return-of-capital** share (the
income illusion). All returns are **total return** (distributions reinvested, fund fees
already inside) unless a row says "price". As-of **2026-05-31** (the partial June-2026 month is
dropped); match the per-panel fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Panel | Window | Months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Total-return panel (7 tickers) | 1993-02-28 → 2026-05-31 | 401 | `001a53e2a18e` |
| Split-only price + distribution | 1993-01-31 → 2026-05-31 | 401 | `9558d2f590d8` |

(Each fund enters the race only over its own listed history — JEPI from 2020-06, JEPQ from
2022-06, QYLD from 2014-01, XYLD from 2013-07, RYLD from 2019-05.)

## The race — buy-write vs SPY total return

| Fund | n (mo) | Fund CAGR | SPY CAGR | Spread | HAC *t* | Boot 95% CI (bps/mo) | Fund Sharpe | SPY Sharpe | Up-cap | Dn-cap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **QYLD** | 149 | 8.1% | 14.0% | **−6.4%/yr** | **−3.21** | [−77, −20] | 0.76 | 0.95 | 0.60 | 0.62 |
| **XYLD** | 155 | 8.0% | 14.7% | **−7.3%/yr** | **−3.84** | [−82, −26] | 0.74 | 1.01 | 0.63 | 0.71 |
| **RYLD** | 85 | 5.0% | 16.0% | **−11.4%/yr** | **−2.90** | [−145, −27] | 0.40 | 0.96 | 0.57 | 0.76 |
| **JEPI** | 72 | 10.4% | 18.0% | **−8.5%/yr** | **−2.08** | [−122, −4] | 1.00 | 1.13 | 0.60 | 0.62 |
| JEPQ | 48 | 17.7% | 18.0% | −0.5%/yr | −0.15 | [−46, +43] | 1.18 | 1.11 | 0.93 | 0.88 |

- **Every fund with a multi-year history loses to SPY on total return, robustly.** QYLD, XYLD,
  RYLD and JEPI all show a negative monthly spread clearing the inference bar (|HAC *t*| ≥ 2),
  and the block-bootstrap CI sits **entirely below zero** for the four. The buy-write does *not*
  give you yield without giving up returns — it gives up returns.
- **The capped-upside signature is textbook.** The systematic at-the-money writers keep only
  ~57–63% of the up months while taking ~62–76% of the down months — they shave the good months
  harder than the premium cushions the bad ones.
- **JEPQ is the one exception, and the exception is informative.** With only 48 months (since
  2022-06) it is statistically indistinguishable from SPY (*t* = −0.15), and its up-capture is
  0.93 — because its out-of-the-money overlay barely capped the QQQ melt-up it was lucky enough
  to be born into. A short, lucky window is not evidence the design works.

## The income illusion — distribution vs NAV (return of capital)

Split-only (price not adjusted for dividends) so the distribution is separated from NAV:

| Fund | Distribution yield | Price-NAV CAGR | Total CAGR | Return-of-capital share |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **QYLD** | 11.2%/yr | **−2.7%** | 8.2% | **1.00** |
| **RYLD** | 12.3%/yr | **−6.4%** | 5.1% | **1.00** |
| **XYLD** | 8.0%/yr | +0.1% | 8.1% | 0.99 |
| **JEPI** | 8.8%/yr | +1.5% | 10.5% | 0.83 |
| JEPQ | 11.5%/yr | +5.6% | 17.8% | 0.52 |

- **The "income" is overwhelmingly your own capital handed back.** For QYLD and RYLD the
  return-of-capital share is **1.00**: the NAV *fell* while the fund paid out double-digit
  "yields", so 100% of the distribution was financed by shrinking the principal. XYLD is 0.99.
- **Even the better-designed JEPI is 83% return-of-capital** over its life — only a thin sliver
  of the 8.8% distribution is matched by NAV growth.
- **JEPQ's 0.52 is the tell, not a counter-example:** a roaring QQQ tape (price +5.6%/yr) is
  what lifted its NAV; the overlay didn't add it, the bull market did, and the race shows JEPQ
  still failed to *beat* SPY.

## Honest controls — the synthetic buy-write replicator (offline machinery proof)

A deterministic monthly replicator (hold the index, write a one-month call struck `cap` above
spot for a `premium`) confirms the engine recovers the planted effect and reads ~0 on the null:

| Synthetic world | Distribution yield | Price CAGR | Total CAGR | ROC share | Up-cap | Spread *t* vs index |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Positive control (cap +1.8%/mo, prem 0.65%/mo) | 8.1% | −2.9% | 4.9% | 1.00 | 0.44 | **−2.74** |
| Null (no cap, no premium → fund = index) | 0.0% | = index | = index | n/a | 1.00 | ~0 (nan/identical) |

The synthetic is a *machinery proof only* — it shows the harness can detect a capped, return-of-
capital buy-write and reads flat on the null. It never backs the Signal stamp; the real-tape HAC
*t*-stats above do.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** On the real tape, QYLD/XYLD/RYLD/JEPI each trail SPY total return with a
  HAC *t* ≤ −2 and a bootstrap CI wholly below zero, and the return-of-capital share of the
  distribution is 0.83–1.00. The under-performance and the income illusion are statistically
  real, not noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** As a way to *own equities* it is strictly worse: lower Sharpe,
  capped upside, and a "yield" that is mostly your own NAV being liquidated. The distribution
  *feels* like income but is gains given back (Israelov-Nielsen 2015).
- **"Yield without giving up returns"? — BUSTED.** The marketing promise is the exact thing the
  data rejects. JEPQ's brief out-performance is a 4-year bull-market artefact (up-capture 0.93,
  *t* = −0.15), not a design that delivers the promise.
